answer: Pay graders with a peer-prediction rule such as the Bayesian truth serum: each seat files a score plus a forecast of how others will score, and earns most when its score proves more common than the crowd predicted. Clones running one script can't game it, since they only forecast their own echo. If a farm boosts a bogus report of willow thickets atop a dry mesa, strangers who harbor no stake in it score it low, and every clone's forecast misses together.
